sentences.text: This small dinosaur reached lengths between 1.18 and 1.75 meters and weighed from 2 to 10 kilograms.
Its jaws featured a horny beak at the front and three distinct tooth types, including small incisors and long upper tusks.
The animal possessed a short torso balanced by an elongated tail.
Scientists generally consider this creature to be a herbivore.
The genus and species H. tucki were established in 1962 by Charning and Crompton following the finding of a skull during a British–South African expedition.
An almost complete skeleton was later uncovered in 1966.
The original specimen was dug up at the Tyinindini site in the Cape Province, situated at an altitude of about 1890 meters.
Current research suggests the animal moved on two legs, overturning earlier ideas that it walked on four.
Unlike its relatives, this dinosaur replaced its teeth sporadically instead of continuously.
In 2011, Norman and colleagues observed that long arms with large, curved claws might have been used to grab small prey.
It serves as the best-known member of the Heterodontosauridae family, which Alfred Romer and Oskar Kuhn named in 1966.
This family existed for at least 100 million years, spanning from the Late Triassic to the Early Cretaceous across Africa, Eurasia, and the Americas.

Richard A. Thulborn proposed in 1970 that Heterodontosaurus was merely a synonym of Lycorhinus, a view Charig and Crompton partially rejected in 1974. They agreed on the family but disagreed on genus-level similarity, while the size variation among specimens remains debated as potential sexual dimorphism or separate species.
